chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad together from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) about a man who deposited with another man one thousand dirhams, which were then lost. The first man said, 'It was a deposit with me,' and the other said, 'It was merely a loan from you.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The money remains with the depositor unless he produces evidence that it was a deposit.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on lost deposited money if the owner cannot prove it was a deposit?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the default presumption of ownership (*asl al-milkiyyah*) in favor of the depositor when the nature of the financial transaction is disputed. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the burden of proof (*al-bayyinah*) lies with the party claiming a change in the legal status of the funds, thereby protecting the depositor’s rights unless the holder can substantiate the claim of a loan (*qard*).
